summary: Wooden 1881 tower on Prince Edward Island's southeast tip; its Marconi station is said to have heard the Titanic's distress call; moved back from the eroding cliff in 1947 and 2014-15.

notes_for_editor: Mostly modern secondary sources (Lighthouse Friends, PEI Lighthouse Society); no NRHP-style nomination or 1881-1899 reports in corpus (marine_ca starts 1900). The Society page appears to mix Panmure Island text with Cape Bear; only the Munn..Keeping paragraphs were used. Keeper order/dates conflict: Lighthouse Friends Jorden 1905-1912, Hyde 1912-1924, White 1924-26; Society has White dying 1925; provincial record names Abraham Daly 1887-1896 (unverified). Titanic claim is unverified by period documents. Record height 12.0 m vs 12.4 m LHF; focal height 16.7 m (record) vs 22.6 m (LHF). Lighthouse Friends says owned by Canadian Coast Guard while record says Northumberland Development Corp; visiting hours may be outdated. Marine report citations are the volumes labelled 1902/1905/1910 in the corpus; the 1906-volume label for the Marconi report and fiscal year should be checked. Page numbers 119, 253 (printed ?), 95 taken from corpus grep; p. 253 and scan p.246 for 1903 list not image-checked. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Marine report fiscal years confirmed (1910 improvements = year ended 31 March 1910; 1905 wireless report = year ended 30 June 1905; keeper list in 1903 volume = 1902 report). Harris and Jordan appointment dates read row-wise in OCR, corroborated by Lighthouse Friends; page images not viewed. Lighthouse Digest gives Titanic year as 1914 (slip) and automation 1960.
